impact: The plan has not solved the sourceVersion problem; it moved it to T-012. Section 4 establishes that ccusage is a black box and that stable or copied input bytes do not prove which bytes it consumed, but section 10.1 claimed T-012 can produce truthful consumed-offset provenance — and T-012 also uses ccusage and explicitly defers owned parsing to v0.5, so its shadows and watermarks prove what was supplied, not what was consumed. Implementing it literally either leaves repeated refresh impossible or publishes fabricated dominance claims. FILED AS ISS-075 (critical) because the contradiction is cross-ticket and contract-level, not a defect in this plan: T-010 requires consumed offsets, no v0.2 ticket can produce them, and resolving it means either redefining sourceVersion as a verified input watermark (updating T-010's contracts and tests) or accepting that repeated authoritative refresh waits for owned parsing. The plan now WITHDRAWS the T-012 claim entirely and claims nothing about what completes the cycle; T-011 remains implementable under either answer, publishing one bootstrap generation and shipping the replacement mechanism.
resolution:
Resolved 2026-08-05 as a historical complaint about superseded plan text, with the underlying contract question answered elsewhere. This issue recorded that T-011's plan (§10.1, revision 6) relocated the sourceVersion problem to T-012 — a ticket structurally unable to solve it. That relocation no longer exists in any live document, and the issue's own impact text already recorded the withdrawal at filing time ('The plan now WITHDRAWS the T-012 claim entirely').

VERIFIED IN THE CURRENT PLAN: docs/t011-headless-service-plan.md §10.1 states verbatim 'And the claim that T-012 completes this is WITHDRAWN — filed as ISS-075' (:1100) and 'this plan claims nothing about what completes repeated refresh' (:1109-1110). The relocation cannot quietly return, because the question it relocated has since been ANSWERED rather than left homeless: N-009 (docs/snapshot-facts-and-watermarks.md v2) redefined sourceVersion as per-surface recency watermarks with separate coverage attestation, and T-025 owns the implementation (parked on ISS-090/ISS-091). The plan's §12 item 5 (rewritten 2026-08-05, :1298) records the final state: ISS-075 NARROWS T-011 to one bootstrap publish; repeated authoritative refresh is T-025's contract, an owner-decided assignment to a ticket that CAN carry it — categorically different from the revision-6 handoff to T-012 this issue caught. See ISS-075's resolution for the full decision record.

RESIDUAL, NAMED SO IT DOES NOT VANISH: T-012's own ticket text (.story/tickets/T-012.json) still carries pre-decision vocabulary at two sites — the merge-contract bullet's 'per-source watermarks (expressed in the same per-source-offset vocabulary as T-010's manifest…)' and AC 8 / the pricing bullet's 'records ccusage version + pricing fetch time', which names a field (ccusageFetchedAt) that T-026 deleted in favor of ccusageInvokedAt. Neither is a consumed-offset CLAIM — this issue's defect does not recur — but both will mislead an implementer. Per the standing rule that a re-plan's first act is repairing its own ticket text (the N-009 runway applied it to T-025 and T-011 already), these two sites belong on T-012's repair list when it re-plans.

Closed with verification attached rather than silently; the recorded reasoning stays — the reviewer's six-round isolation of the supplied-vs-consumed substitution is preserved here, in ISS-075, and in the plan's own retained blockquotes (the plan's convention is that superseded arguments stay visible, and §12 item 5's original verdict is kept in a blockquote at :1318).
